name: SikaTile-110 Secure Proof
paste:
SIKATILE®-110 SECURE PROOF: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof, September 2026, Version 02.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sikatile-110-secureproof.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2026, Version 02.01).
1.2 Product description.
    - A premium performance, flexible class III, ready to use, water based polyurethane waterproofing membrane designed for internal and external areas including wet areas, balconies, terraces, and non UV exposed above ground external applications.
    - SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof is a suitable undertile waterproofing membrane that complies to AS/NZS 4654:2012 and AS 4858:2004.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof is suitable for use on walls and floors for both internal and external applications including under pedistall and paver applications. SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof is suitable for most typical construction substrates such as.
    - Concrete
    - GRC - Glass reinforced concrete
    - Cement boards and sheets including Scyon
    - Renders and screeds
    - Cement coated light weight construction boards
    - Plasterboard
    - Structural Plywood
    - Autoclaved Aerated Concrete (AAC)
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: A PREMIUM PERFORMANCE, CLASS III, READY TO USE, WATER-BASED POLYURETHANE WATERPROOFING MEMBRANE DESIGNED FOR UNDER TILE AND STONE APPLICATIONS.
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer - Branz as/nzs 4858:2004. Test Certificate DC13205-003
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS/NZS 4654:2012: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Description (p.1).
    - AS 4858:2004: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Description (p.1).
    - SCAQMD method 304-91: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Product Information > Volatile organic compound (VOC) content (p.1).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Premixed, ready to use
    - High extensibility, Class III
    - Class III flexible performance
    - UV Stable - suitable for non trafficable areas.
    - Solvent free, water-based
    - Excellent antifracture properties
    - Excellent cure time
    - Low VOC
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Colour: Grey
    - Volatile organic compound (VOC) content: 62g/L (SCAQMD method 304-91)
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Tensile strength: 2.1MPa
    - Permeability to water vapour: 1.55g/m² / 24 hours
2.7 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 15 Litre Pail / 32 Pails per pallet
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of manufacture when stored unopened in elevated, cool, dry location.
    - Storage conditions: Store in dry cool conditions out of direct sunlight. Do not allow membrane to freeze.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2026, Version 02.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality.
    - All surfaces must be installed according to manufacturer’s instructions and relevant Australian Standard(s) and be structurally sound, dry, clean and free from movement, oil, grease, wax, curing compounds, release agents and any other loose or contaminating material.
    - Prior to application, remove all sharp protrusions, which may pierce the membrane
    - Any voids, potholes in the substrate must be appropriately filled up with a high strength mortar refer to Sika Monotop® mortars.
3.3 Substrate quality - Concrete.
    - All new concrete slabs must have a wood float finish and be allowed to cure for 28 days. (refer to priming details for early aged concrete)
    - Old concrete must be cleaned with a strong commercial grade detergent or degreaser. Residue must then be thoroughly washed off with clean water. Allow the surface to dry for at least 24 hours
    - All laitance and efflorescence must be removed prior to application.
3.4 Substrate quality - Cement based Renders & Screeds.
    - Renders and screeds should have a wood float finish and be allow to cure for 5-7. (refer priming details for early aged green screeds)
3.5 Substrate quality - Cement Boards and Sheets.
    - All boards and sheet shall be installed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions and be specifically designed for tiling applications.
    - Screw and nail heads must be treated with a Sika® Neutral cure silicone or Sika® Fillet Joint.
    - All sheet joints, seams, penetrations, and wall floor junctions shall have a Sika® Neutral cure silicone, Sikaflex® Fillet Joint or Sika SealTape F flexible waterproofing bandage.
3.6 Substrate preparation - Substrate Priming Chart.
    | Application | Primer |
    | Dry porous substrates | SikaTile 010 Secure Prime |
    | Damp subtrates with RH >75% and early ageas screed | Sikalastic Moisture Seal |
3.7 Substrate preparation - Early aged (green) screeds Sikalastic® Moisture Seal.
    | Existing tiles | Sikafloor-14 Prep n Prime Impact |
    | Non-porous Substrates ie: | SikaFloor-14 Prep n Prime |
    | PVC, Metal and Waterstop Angles | Impact |
    Refer to the primer data sheet for additional information.
3.8 Substrate preparation - Static Cracks - not subject to movement.
    - Small hairline cracks, up to 1mm wide, may be filled by the first application of SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof
    - For cracks / joints wider than 1mm, a joint filler should be applied along the length of the crack prior to the application of SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof
    Non Dymanic Cracks - less than 3mm subject to movement
    All cracks / joints, irrespective of their width, must be filled firstly with the bond breaker sealant. Then
    50mm wide polyethylene / polypropylene tape should be placed over the crack, ensuring it adheres to the surface. Apply the SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof over the tape as per installation instructions.
3.9 Substrate preparation - Bond Breaker. SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof has high extensibility and is designed for use with a 12 mm bond breaker, a bead of Sika® Neutral cure silicone, Sika® Fillet Joint or a suitable Sika® flexible waterproofing bandage. The sealant applied must be tooled off to form a 12 mm wide bond breaker. A bond breaker must be installed at areas subject to movement, wall/wall junction, wall/floor junction, sheet joints and seams, penetrations and where there is a change in the direction or substrate type.
3.10 Substrate preparation - Falls to Drains. All areas shall have falls in accordance with National Construction Code (NCC) requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (September 2026, Version 02.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Consumption: The minimum dry film thickness required is 1.0mm applied in a minimum 2 coat installation. A 15 Litre pail will cover 10m²
4.3 Applied product ready for use. Drying Time
    | Ready for 2nd coat | 1-2 hours after 1st coat |
    | Ready for tiling | 6-8 hours after final coat |
    | Ready for flood testing | 48 hours |
    | Return to service | 3+ days |
    All measurements are taken at 23°C and 50% relative humidity. Specifications vary according to site conditions and should be taken as a guide only.
4.4 Equipment.
    - Brush, or short nap roller
    - Protective personal equipment
4.5 Application method / tools - Standard Application.
    - 1. SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof requires no mixing. Apply directly from the pail. Use a brush or roller to apply the first coat of SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof on the area to be waterproofed. 2. Allow the first coat to dry for approximately 2- 3 hours before applying the 2nd coat at 90° to the first coat. Ensure there are no imperfections on the waterproofing membrane. 3. Apply a third coat if necessary or required to do so. The minimum dry film thinkness shall be 1.00mm 4. Allow the final coat to dry for at least 8 hours prior to tiling application
    - Application under Pedestall & Paver application 1. SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof requires no mixing. Apply directly from the pail. Use a brush or roller to apply the first coat of SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof on the area to be waterproofed. 2. Allow the first coat to dry for approximately 2-3 hours before applying the 2nd coat at 90° to the first coat. Ensure there are no imperfections on the waterproofing membrane. 3. Apply a third coatas (as additional wear layer for pedestall and paver application. 4. The minimum dry film thickness for under pedestall and paver shall be 1.6mm 5. Allow the final coat to dry for at least 24 hours prior to pedestall and paver application
    - Drying times are influence by factors beyond the control of the manufacturer, use drying times as a guide only.
4.6 Application method / tools - Flood testing (if required).
    - Allow SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof to dry and cure for a minimum 72 hours at 23°C and 50% relative humidity for standard applications, and 96 hours at 23°C and 50% relative humidity for paver and pedestall application.
    - Conduct flood test for 24 hours at max 50mm depth with water.
    - Inspect membrane for water loss, release water and allow area to dry prior prior to subsequent coatings
    - Repair membrane if required.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment immediately after us with water. Once cured, residual material can only be removed mechanically.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof is not suitable for applications in areas of permanent water immersion.
    - SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof is not suitable for applications in area of negative hydrostatic pressure or rising damp. Seek sika technical advice.
    - Delay applications if rain or inclement weather is imminent.
    - SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof must be applied at the recommended coverage rates.
    - Tongue & groove timber flooring must be over sheeted with fibre cement sheeting or ceramic tile underlay.
    - Partical board flooring shall be adequately prepared with all contaminates removed and over sheeted with a suitable ceramic tile underlay or reinforced screed.
    - To minimise the chance of damage install finished covering as soon as possible once the membrane has cured.
    - SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof must not be used as a wearing surface for foot and vehicular traffic.
    - Contact Sika® for information or applications not mentioned in the document.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. 5°C to 35°C
5.3 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Delay applications if rain or inclement weather is imminent.
5.4 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Conduct flood test for 24 hours at max 50mm depth with water.
5.5 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.6 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof, September 2026, Version 02.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/p/sikatile-110-secureproof.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaTile®-110 Secure Proof, version 07/10/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/t/sds-sikatile-110secureproof.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
